correctness.rationale: The normalized b_chi Fourier basis is legitimate because |A| is a unit after splitting. Direct change of variables gives b_i b_j=b_{tau(i)} exactly when j=sigma(i), otherwise zero, where tau and sigma are bijections by the Latin condition. In each zero-product Leibniz equation, the coefficients of b_{tau(sigma^{-1}(j))} and b_{tau(i)} must vanish separately since their indices differ. Taking j=sigma(k) for k!=i annihilates every off-diagonal D(b_i) coefficient. Nonzero-product equations yield the stated necessary and sufficient character-indexed linear relation. Faithful scalar extension makes the commutator vanish over K. For A=F_p, diagonalization by multiplicative characters reduces to eta(t)+eta(1-t)=1; unit-modulus root geometry forces conjugate primitive sixth roots and 6|(p-1), with (p-1)/3 for t^2-t+1=0. Independently rebuilt all p^2-variable Leibniz constraints for p=3,5,7 and compared their modular ranks with the p-variable diagonal system: all admissible parameters agree. The auxiliary-modulus rank experiment is not the general proof.

value.rationale: Derivation Lie algebras encode infinitesimal symmetries of nonassociative algebras; this complete finite-Latin classification gives an abelianity theorem and sparse character-kernel reduction for every finite abelian A, and identifies the unexpected first nonrigid seven-point prime-cyclic examples. Those are structurally motivated facts, not an arbitrary small enumeration.
